thread:
Ana L.: quick update — ran CPU-side profiling on the staging inference worker (8xA100, 4 shards) to look at tokenization + scheduler delay that was causing 95th pct tail spikes.
Michael K.: nice — which tools did you use? perf or py-spy / flamegraphs?
Ana L.: perf record + flamegraph for native stacks, and py-spy sampling to get Python hot paths. also used perf script + stackcollapse-perf.pl -> flamegraph.pl for visual.
Ana L.: command I ran:
```sh
perf record -F 99 -g --python -o perf.data -- sleep 30 
perf script -i perf.data | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
./flamegraph.pl out.folded > perf-tokenizer.svg
py-spy record -o pyspy.svg --native --subprocess -p $PID --duration 30
```
Jessie P.: link to artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/1744559001/perf-tokenizer.svg and s3://redwood-perf/1744559001/pyspy.svg :eyes:
Sanjay R.: quick notes from the flame: big wedge on Python side is `tokenizer.py:tokenize_batch` and `scheduler.py:acquire_batch_lock` — looks like we hold the batch lock while doing tokenization for some inputs.
Michael K.: holding lock during tokenization explains misaligned batching: other requests wait and form tiny batches, causing more frequent kernel launches.
Ana L.: exact. measured ~18% CPU time in `tokenizer.py` and ~12% in the lock path. native stacks show syscalls around memcpy for protobuf serialize when updating KV cache.
Sanjay R.: pasted perf top snippet:
```
  15.0%  runtime/python  [.] tokenizer.py:tokenize_batch
  12.3%  runtime/python  [.] scheduler.py:acquire_batch_lock
   8.7%  runtime/libc     [.] memcpy
   6.1%  runtime/python  [.] kv_cache.py:serialize_update
   4.2%  runtime/python  [.] batching.py:flush_when_full
```
Jessie P.: interestingly py-spy shows many short-lived frames from `c_extensions._tokenize` — so some tokenization already in C, but Python wrapper still dominates.
Ana L.: hypothesis: tokenization heavy path still does Python-level looping for special-casing (unicode normalization + fallback) which amplifies GIL hold time.
Michael K.: what about moving expensive stable normalization into the C extension and only returning bytes? Also pipeline pre-tokenization for repeated prompt templates.
Sanjay R.: +1. Another low-effort win: reduce lock scope — acquire batch lock only to append IDs and metadata, release, then do tokenization asynchronously per-worker. That will reduce contention for the scheduler.
Ana L.: did a quick patch: move KV cache proto serialization off the hot path into a background IO thread (persist_queue). local test dropped `kv_cache.py:serialize_update` from 6.1% -> 1.4% and reduced syscalls (memcpy) bursts. tail latency improved ~18% on p50->p95 in synthetic replay.
Michael K.: nice. did you re-run perf to confirm new flame?
Ana L.: yes — new flamegraph shows split: tokenization remains but lock wedge shrinks. py-spy confirms more time in C tokenization frames.
Jessie P.: any perf regressions on the C kernel side (CUDA) when these changes applied? we need to ensure we didn't increase GPU kernel variance by changing request timing.
Ana L.: good point — ran nsys short traces. CUDA kernel timelines showed slightly more compact dispatch (fewer micro-batches) which reduced kernel launch overhead overall. no regressions in average GPU utilization, and kernel durations stable. nsys artifact: s3://redwood-perf/1744559001/nsys-trace.qdrep
Sanjay R.: follow-ups: 1) add unit perf test that exercises heavy unicode cases; 2) prototype pre-tokenize cache keyed by template hash; 3) instrument scheduler metrics for lock wait time per-route.
Michael K.: agree. add an opt-in config so Dedicated customers can enable pre-tokenize to avoid breaking behavior.
Ana L.: I'll open PR with three commits: (a) reduce lock scope in scheduler, (b) background KV serialization, (c) move normalization into C extension (proto API change). will include perf artifacts and before/after flame images.
perf-bot: perf check complete — baseline p95=142ms, patched p95=116ms (18% improvement). full report: https://internal-perf/reports/1744559001
Jessie P.: can you also add a small benchmark that runs with `-j 8` worker threads to show multi-thread scaling? we had some cases where mania of threads + GIL made things worse.
Ana L.: yes, will include thread scaling matrix. finishing PR description now. cc @Michael K., @Sanjay R. for review.
Michael K.: thanks — once merged, let's run nightly replay on staging for 24h to watch for rare regressions. :thumbsup:
Sanjay R.: and maybe add a short perf lab doc describing how to interpret py-spy vs perf differences for tokenization vs native memcpy hotspots. saved time last week.
Ana L.: will draft that too. thanks all!
